info.title: Armada shared control API
info.description: Generated integration REST contracts. Includes SDK operations and shared-tool routes. Administrative and provider-specific extensions are outside this description. Files use sandbox/exec; this description does not assert provider availability.

post.description: Reads the selected provider adapter's golden capacity without creating an App or resource. Null is unknown/unbounded, not a workspace quota.
Dry-run first: select an existing visible golden by id. Confirm with the returned receipt within ten minutes. Preserves all rows and ACLs.

Configure or refresh the owner's GitHub access in a running sandbox without relaunching. Enrolled Armada runtimes use current-epoch private RPC; native Boat keeps its existing setup. Reuses a validated unexpired token; rejection/expiry can require renewal. Only the sandbox owner may request this.

post.description: Owner-only non-secret current-epoch configuration and credential-request count. Does not return credentials or probe GitHub.

post.description: Collects one bounded read-only VM observation and reports the last ten comparable repository sessions. Missing evidence causes abstention; never resizes or changes defaults.

post.description: Gives the agent its next instruction as a new turn. Without conversation_id the first send of an idle sandbox opens a conversation and later sends continue the latest one. To redirect a turn that is still running, use steer. The turn runs with the model and effort chosen at launch; model and reasoning_effort override them for this turn only. Experimental runtime follow-up requires request_id, an empty ready sandbox, existing conversation, or verified empty checkpoint; retained idle pauses wake automatically before expiry. Preserved stopped Boat/Modal sandboxes resume on send; terminal sandboxes refuse controls with recovery guidance. Model/effort remain pinned to launch.

id.description: Armada's sandbox id (a uuid, as returned by launch and list).

request_id.description: Required for runtime follow-up; reuse with identical input after uncertain delivery. Native providers accept the field for compatibility only; they do not deduplicate.

conversation_id.description: A conversation of the sandbox. Default: the latest.

model.description: The model, by id. claude: claude-opus-5-5 (low|medium|high|xhigh|max), claude-sonnet-5-5 (low|medium|high|xhigh|max); default claude-opus-5-5 medium. codex: gpt-6.2-sol (low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra), gpt-6.2-astra (low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra), gpt-6.1-sol (low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra), gpt-6.1-terra (low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra), gpt-6-astra (low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra), gpt-6-sol (low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra), gpt-6-luna (low|medium|high|xhigh|max); default gpt-6.2-sol medium. opencode: armada/deepseek-flash (default); default armada/deepseek-flash default.

reasoning_effort.description: The reasoning effort; one the model accepts (see model).

post.description: Owner-only. Restarts the same Docker allocation with fresh runtime enrolment, keeping history and the original TTL. Reuse request_id after uncertainty.

id.description: Armada's sandbox id (a uuid, as returned by launch and list).

post.description: Quiesce and seal the current Boat runtime journal/harness state before compute stop. Does not stop the VM or promise disk retention/resume. Owner-only; reuse request_id on uncertainty. New sends remain fenced until fresh enrolment.

id.description: Armada's sandbox id (a uuid, as returned by launch and list).

post.description: Activates the retained sandbox under a fresh epoch and verifies its sealed checkpoint. Continues the saved native conversation, or starts the first only from a verified empty journal. Owner-only; stable request_id, no implicit retry of uncertain activation. Cached outcome is historical, not current machine state.

post.description: Explicit result for the latest finished turn. Call after wait; never inferred from message text. A new send clears it. Only the sandbox owner or current org admin may report or read it.

post.description: Stops the machine. Modal keeps its disk only if checkpoint succeeds; fallback termination returns checkpoint_failed_disk_not_retained and cannot resume. Other retained stops can resume on send. Use it when the agent is done, so the sandbox stops costing.

id.description: Armada's sandbox id (a uuid, as returned by launch and list).

post.description: Set a later expiry, measured from now. Owner/admin only. Modal extensions must fit inside the current physical machine lifetime; stop and resume for a new physical lifetime.

post.description: Owner/admin only. Permanently removes provider resources and recovery archives. Stop first. Legacy orchestrator parents and children are refused; ordinary delegated children require a deleted parent.

post.description: Blocks until the agent settles (its turn finished, failed or was interrupted, or the machine stopped) or the timeout passes, then answers like status with timedOut. Default 60s, at most 600s: call again to keep waiting.

post.description: Forks a golden into a new sandbox, pulls its repos, runs its init commands, and starts the agent. With `prompt` the agent starts working at once (status running). Without it the sandbox is left ready and the conversation starts at the first `send`. The sandbox gets only your (or your org's) Armada credentials for this agent, never the boat.dev account's. When the caller connected GitHub, git and gh in the sandbox act as that person (8 hour token): see `github` in the answer. Setup can take a few minutes.

idempotencyKey.description: Reuse this key for retries; inspect launch_receipt after an unknown outcome.

externalRef.description: Opaque caller reference, for example one business object id. Not unique; use idempotencyKey for exactly-once.

golden.description: The golden's name, as in golden_list.

provider.description: The golden's provider. Needed only when the name exists on several providers.

model.description: The model, by id. claude: claude-opus-5-5 (low|medium|high|xhigh|max), claude-sonnet-5-5 (low|medium|high|xhigh|max); default claude-opus-5-5 medium. codex: gpt-6.2-sol (low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra), gpt-6.2-astra (low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra), gpt-6.1-sol (low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra), gpt-6.1-terra (low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra), gpt-6-astra (low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra), gpt-6-sol (low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra), gpt-6-luna (low|medium|high|xhigh|max); default gpt-6.2-sol medium. opencode: armada/deepseek-flash (default); default armada/deepseek-flash default.

repo.description: Configured directory or owner/repo from the golden. Prepares native agent cwd, including idle launches. Not confinement.

prompt.description: The first instruction. Leave out for an idle sandbox.

ttlSeconds.description: Seconds before the machine stops by itself. Default 14400 (4 hours). At most 2592000 (30 days) on boat, 86400 (24 hours) on modal; a longer TTL is refused.

reasoningEffort.description: The reasoning effort; one the model accepts (see model).

schema.description: REST launch receipt: sandbox, golden, promptId, conversationId, ttlSeconds, expiresAt, github and helper. Provider records may carry additional fields.

post.description: Launch an immutable template revision. requestKey is required: same key/body returns the recorded request and never allocates twice. Readable variables are NOT secrets; no secret bindings or authority-enlarging overrides.

The agent's events oldest first: prompts (with status and failure reason), messages and tool calls, steers. The default is one bounded page (100 events). Set all to read every available page (up to 100 pages) in one response. Pass the returned cursor as since_cursor to read only what is new. An event read twice has the same id and the newer body; each id appears once per response.

id.description: Armada's sandbox id (a uuid, as returned by launch and list).

all.description: Read all available pages, bounded at 100 pages.

cursor.description: The cursor of the previous page.

conversationId.description: A conversation of the sandbox. Default: the latest.

follow.description: Follow events within the bounded HTTP request.

code.description: Public failure code; clients must tolerate future codes.
